rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Summary 1.1 Actions 1.2 Cleanup phase 1.3 Final Scoring 1.4 Strategy Tips 2 Italian (original) Summary The game is divided into five rounds, after which the game ends. In each round, players will take at least four actions. Up to four more extra actions per round can be acquired by building preacher (brown) and different residence (purple) cards. Points are earned by building Monuments (bronze-colored cards) from a common pool, and district buildings (blue grey and green cards) that are dealt into your hand. Monuments and blue/green buildings all require hiring an artist (also from common pool), which must be an acceptable type (painter, sculptor, or architect), and typically adds points to the construction. Constructing buildings requires having sufficient resources (six different types), and enough money (fiorini) (for the artist, and often also the building!). Location cards (light grey) on the table are actions that can be used once per round. They are the primary way to acquire resources (apart from income during cleanup phase). There are also locations for exchanging resources, becoming Captain of the People (first player), and for selling resources. Actions Players get four actions per round (one in each of the first four phases of the round), plus additional actions (in subsequent phases) from purple and brown cards (up to four more). Actions are: - Activate a location card (light grey) - Play a Florenza card to your tableau (building a card from hand) - Build a Monument - Reserve a Monument or Artist - Send out workers (+50 fiorini) - Go to the market (buy or sell a resource for 100, or trade 2 resources for 1) - Look for inspiration (draw a Florenza card) Cleanup phase After each round: - players discard all but one card from their hand, then draw back up to five total, then: -- each constructed residence (purple) gives a player one more card draw - sweep and refill the artists and (most of) the monuments on the table: -- the two highest valued monuments remain between rounds - players receive income: -- 200 fiorini, 1 marble, 1 wood -- all workshops they have built -- one resource chosen by the current round's Captain (first player) - Captain of the People (first-player) marker moves to whoever used that location card, or else rotates. - Restore location cards (turn face up) Final Scoring After the fifth round's action phase has ended, final scoring. - constructed monuments, district buildings, and their artists all score the number shown in top right corner - complete sets of district buildings (one each of blue, grey, green) score additional 5 points - some guilds (orange) cards have their own scoring conditions - There will be a final production after the last round, then money and resources are scored: -- the player with the most money earns 4 points, second 2 points, third 1 point. -- the player with the most resources earns 4 points, second 2 points, third 1 point. - player who was captain of the people scores 1 point Note: - reserved artists and monuments that were not constructed are negative points! Strategy Tips - first two rounds, it's especially important to get production and extra-actions cards played (get your engine going!) -- workshops (mustard-yellow cards) produce every round -- residences (purple) and preachers (brown) provide extra actions each round -- note, there are three different residence types, each providing another action! - (generally) don't reserve artists or monuments -- actions are too precious! - after you figure out what you can build in a round, and acquire the resources necessary, extra actions should be used grabbing any resources still available from locations before you do the building. building should generally be your last actions of the round. -- playing purple/brown cards gives you extra actions the same round -- order them carefully! Implementation is rather unforgiving. Be sure to double check your plan before you take action. Italian (original) Il turno di gioco si divide in 4 fasi: Pesca degli Artisti e dei Monumenti Pesca delle carte Florenza Azioni (4 per round più eventuali azioni extra ottenute dalle carte giocate) Giocare una carta Florenza Realizzare un Monumento Riservarsi un Monumento o un Artista Attivare una carta centrale (raccogli/vendi le risorse indicate da una carta che sia sul tavolo a faccia in su) Mandare fuori un lavoratore a giornata (raccogli 50 Fiorini) Andare al Mercato (vendi/compra/scambia risorse con la riserva) Cercare ispirazione (pesca una carta Florenza extra) Operazioni di Fine turno Scartare tutte le carte Monumento rimaste sul tavolo, tranne le due più a sinistra Scartare tutte le carte Artista rimaste eventualmente in gioco Scartare tutte le carte Florenza in mano ai giocatori, tranne una a scelta del giocatore Distribuire le rendite Eleggere il nuovo Capitano del Popolo Ripristinare le carte centrali Fine della partita dopo 5 turni.

[Rating: 2/10] All the worst parts of eurogames made into one game without anything redeeming. It even has unnecessary luck factor in it.

[Rating: 2/10] Many better collection games out there. No reason to play again. Seems too random. Artwork uninteresting.

[Rating: 2.5/10] Mediocre game with an economic engine seen a hundred times before. Get resources and build things that either get you more ressources or victory points. This alone would not result in my bad rating but the game has a major flaw: You start with 4 actions per round. The purple cards will allow you to boost this up to 8 actions per round (in a 5 round game). In our 4 player game we had two players going up to six actions right in round one to then boost it up to 7 actions in the second round. For this you just need to be lucky enough to get them drawn. [Rating: 4/10] I really wanted to like this game. Even though the theme is completely generic, I always wanted to try Florenza, but its price and complexity I found too daunting. I was hoping that the card game would be more accessible. But it felt weird, very sprawling and clunky. Like you can take all kinds of cards and make them work together. There were so many cards that it became fruitless to even look at what your opponent was doing, which in a 2-player game like I tried, must be a bad thing. It felt too open-ended, more like building with Legos rather than playing a game.

[Rating: 4/10] Just recently started playing Florenza: The Card Game. I have not played Florenza, so I can't compare it. Anyway, I find the game to be quite fun. Not bad with two but better with more, as the battle for resources, etc. is tighter. I like how it requires you to think a few turns ahead as you build up your resources for whatever you plan to build. Sort of a slow burn. I think the art really matches the theme of the game. It's not easy to find as Miniature Market and Cool Stuff do not seem to have it listed.

[Rating: 4/10] It's a bit odd. This game feels very solitair despite you being so reliant on what the other players do. Probably due to the importance of those hand cards that you're sneakily striving towards. Also, might make it more interactive if you play with open resources (so you know who might be aiming for what monuments). Scores are surprisingly closes usually which is not really a good thing here. Due to the way how artist cards work this means many a game can be determined by the luck of your (artist) draw.

[Rating: 4/10] TRADED IT! (For City Tycoon)  The game works and has all the trappings of a classic "resource to victory points in a small number of turns" Euro. The problem is other games do it way better without the fussy pile of cards all over and needless upkeep of dealing out card rows and managing draw piles. It also suffers from the fact there is little tension, as most goals produce roughly the same points. [Rating: 5/10] On one hand Florenza is a fairly meaty economic development and engine building game, on the other it's a highly luck-driven card game. Those two qualities are obviously very much at odds with each other, and the strategic character of city development never really materializes because you are typically reduced to playing the exact hand you get dealt each turn. The way the extra actions are handled and the missing lookahead from turn to turn strongly tilt the game balance towards the lucky draw.

[Rating: 5/10] Too random, though you might not notice it for a few plays. The cards that give extra actions are so much better than the others, even better than income cards, because you can use extra action for income or for something else. Yet you might never see any of them. Mixing deck eras together before dealing is exactly backwards too -- try getting nothing but era I cards when the opponents are getting era III cards, but it's quite possible.
